## Keywords

{{< glossary app-package process loading gpu refresh-rate resolution latency cloud-gaming thermal-throttling >}}

## 2.1 From the store to the first frame

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- A game comes as one file: an **APK** on Android, an **IPA** on iPhone.
- Installing copies the game into **storage**.
- Launching loads it into **memory**. The running game is a **process**.
- When memory is full, the system closes games in the background.
- **Do it:** Time a game start on your phone, from the icon to the menu.
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
![](images/launch.png)
:::
::::

## Example · Cheap phone, slow loading

A level has 1500 MB of assets. A fast phone reads 1500 MB per second; a cheap
phone reads 150 MB per second. **How long does the level load on each phone?**

::: {.reveal}
1. Fast phone: 1500 MB ÷ 1500 MB per second = **1 second**.
2. Cheap phone: 1500 MB ÷ 150 MB per second = **10 seconds**.
3. The game is the same. Only the slower storage makes it 10 times slower.
:::

## Try it 1 · Install, launch, load

a) A player installs a game. Which part of the phone does it fill?
b) A level has 900 MB of assets. The phone reads 300 MB per second. How many seconds does the level take to load?
c) A game starts again from the title screen after a long break. Why?

::: {.answer}
a) storage
b) 3 seconds (900 ÷ 300)
c) The system closed it to free memory.
:::

## 2.2 The frame on real hardware

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- The **CPU** runs the game logic. The **GPU** draws the pixels.
- The slower of the two sets the frame rate (fps).
- The screen shows at most its **refresh rate** (Hz) in new pictures.
- A phone has no fan. When it gets hot, it slows down (**throttling**).
- **Do it:** On the lab computer, find the resolution and refresh rate of the screen.
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
![](images/cpu-gpu-pipeline.png)
:::
::::

## Try it 2 · Frames, screens, heat

a) Which processor colours the pixels of the picture?
b) The screen shows 120 Hz and the game makes 70 fps. How many new pictures does the player see per second?
c) The chip gets hot and the phone slows down. What is this called?

::: {.answer}
a) the GPU
b) 70
c) thermal throttling
:::

## 2.3 Where the game is computed

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- **Local:** the whole game runs on the device.
- **Client–server:** each device runs the game; a server keeps the shared data.
- **Cloud gaming:** a server runs the game; the phone shows a video.
- **Latency** is the delay between an action and its result. The cloud adds latency.
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
![](images/where-game-runs.png)
:::
::::

## Try it 3 · Near or far?

a) The game runs on a server, and the phone only shows the video. Where is the game computed?
b) What do we call the delay between a tap and the jump on the screen?
c) Which game suffers most from 100 ms of lag: a card game or a fighting game?

::: {.answer}
a) in the cloud (cloud gaming)
b) latency
c) a fighting game
:::

## 2.4 Device classes for gaming

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- **Phone, tablet:** touch, battery, short sessions.
- **PC:** keyboard and mouse, long sessions at a desk.
- **Console:** gamepad and TV, long sessions at home.
- **Cloud:** any screen, but it needs a fast network.
- **Do it:** Choose a game you know. Which device class fits it best, and why?
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
![](images/devices.png)
:::
::::

## Try it 4 · Which device class?

a) A player uses a gamepad and a TV for long sessions at home. Which device class is it?
b) A player has five minutes on the bus, with touch and a battery. Which device class fits?
c) Which device class works on any screen, but only with a fast network?

::: {.answer}
a) console
b) smartphone
c) cloud gaming
:::

## Try it 5 · One game, many devices (harder)

The facts: the cheapest Android phone reads 120 MB per second. One cloud player has a slow connection.

a) How many seconds does a 600 MB level take to load on the cheapest phone?
b) What gets worse for the cloud player with the slow connection?
c) In which device class does heat matter most in a 30-minute session?

::: {.answer}
a) 5 seconds (600 ÷ 120)
b) the latency (input lag)
c) smartphone
:::

## Summary

- Installing copies a game into storage; launching loads it into memory.
- The speed of storage decides the loading time.
- The slower of the CPU and the GPU sets the frame rate.
- A phone slows down when it gets hot (thermal throttling).
- Cloud gaming adds latency and needs a fast Internet connection.
- Each device class needs its own input, screen and play time.
